newsitem.title: USA: Good Buy winners from Good Housekeeping.
newsitem.headline: Good Buy winners from Good Housekeeping.

text.p: Hidden away in an ordinary-looking office building in midtown Manhattan is the Good Housekeeping Institute, where pantyhose stretch, biscuits bake and hair dryers run for hours.

The employees of the Institute push and pull new products to the breaking point. For the second year, they've sorted through close to 1,000 items and selected Good Buy winners, an award given to "problem-solvers that deliver great service, with style."
The winning products are "all things that we already know people need -- they're existing appliances made better," said Sharon Franke, director of the Food Appliances department of the Institute.
All of the winners are new, high quality items and the prices are "not as high as you'd think; within the reach of most people," Franke said.

It was a huge task to sift through all the new products that the Institute evaluates each a year. In selecting the Good Buy winners for this year, Franke said the Institute staff eliminated "gimmicky" items, finally winnowing down the list to nine winners.
All the products are either currently available in department or mass merchandising stores, or can be ordered from the manufacturer.

DuPont's Teflon-coated fabric sheets make any piece of ovenware non-stick. No need to throw out old pots and pans, because the sheets can be trimmed to fit into any piece you have. They are reusable and can be washed by hand or in the dishwasher. A pack of six liners costs $19.95. One 10 inch by 15 inch liner costs $4.95. For more information call 1-800-986-2857.

Sunbeam's Toaster-Logic Toaster has a brain -- a computer chip that monitors temperature and voltage fluctuations and adjusts toasting time for evenly browned bread. Wide slots hold thick bagels. The plastic casing stays cool even when the toaster inside is hot. It costs $39. For information call 1-800-597-5987.

Conair's Cord-Keeper hair dryer does away with twisted or dangling cords. Press a button and the cord is retracted into the handle. The dryer is rated at 1,600 watts so it's powerful enough to dry thick hair. It costs $42.99.

Oxo's Good Grips Tea Kettle is a two-quart whistling kettle that has a curved plastic shield to protect your hand from steam. The handle is well-positioned for pouring, and has a rubber grip that won't heat up. The price of the Oxo kettle ranges from $44.99 for enamel finish to $54.99 for stainless steel. For more information call 1-800-445-6836.
Casio's Phonemate answering machine with pager link combines several functions in one. This Good Buy can also be used as a speakerphone. It costs about $149. For more information call 310-320-9810.

T-Fal, maker of cookware, got a Good Buy award for its Clipso Pressure Cooker. This 6.4 quart stainless steel model is easy to operate. Just press the knob to open or lock. The heavy aluminum base promotes even cooking and safety features prevent bursting. It costs $149. For more information call 1-800-395-8325.

Whirlpool's Accubake gas range has a new heat management system that keeps the temperature as close as possible to the one selected. It has a large oven and sealed gas stove top burners, which prevent food from spilling underneath. Self-cleaning models run about $850. Models with fewer features cost $550 to $750. For more information call 1-800-253-1301.

Frigidaire's Side-by-Side refrigerator combines an ice maker with a Puresource filtered water dispenser. The freezer contains slide-out baskets, a refrigerator shelf flips up to accommodate tall bottles and another pulls out for smaller items. The refrigerators in the Side-by-Side line have 22-square feet to 28-square feet capacities. They range in price from $1,549 to $1,999. For more information call 1-800-451-7007.

A new photo technology, the Advanced Photo System, was given a Good Housekeeping Good Buy award. New pocket sized APS cameras and 24mm film make picture taking super-easy. Film is loaded into the camera as one would put in a battery. Three different photo sizes can be chosen using the same camera or film. A special logo identifies products using this new system. Prices for processing are similar to 35mm cameras, Good Housekeeping said. Cameras and film are available from many manufactrurers, but the magazine highlighted Kodak's Advantix 3200AF, at $119.95, and Fuji film.
The Good Buy awards are highlighted in the magazine's January 1997 edition ($1.95).
